Subject: Aperture - initial rightsizing draft and recommended cutover safety nets

Hi Sam / Neha,

Attached is the first pass rightsizing worksheet (aperture-sizing-sheet.xlsx). Summary below — this is conservative and assumes single-model production (Llama-3-3B quantized) with KV cache enabled.

Summary (phase 1 commit):
- Sustained baseline: 120 RPS -> estimated sustained token throughput ~54k tokens/sec (in+out).
- Burst headroom: plan for +30% -> design target 156 RPS sustained.
- Recommended reserved GPUs: 8x A100-80GB equiv (dedicated pool) with autoscale floor of 6, burst to 10 via reserved burst pool.
- Expected latency at 156 RPS with batching and KV cache: median 140-180ms, 95th ~230-260ms depending on sequence length.
- Suggested batching config: dynamic batching with 40ms max batch delay for interactive flows; background batch windows for job traffic.

Operational guardrails / runbook highlights:
- Canary plan: 10% live traffic for 2 hours with live metrics (token latency, error rate, model cost) -> move to 50% for 4 hours if stable -> full swap.
- Rollback triggers: sustained 95th >350ms for 10 minutes OR error rate >1.5% for 5 minutes -> automatic rollback to hosted routing.
- Blackout window: prefer late-night UTC 02:00-05:00 for full swap to minimize impact; we can also support your Oct 23-27 weekday window if you require business-hours validation.
- Dry run: recommended 72-hour dress rehearsal three business days prior to cutover. We'll lead the rehearsal and assign an ops wing to monitor.

Attachments included:
- aperture-sizing-sheet.xlsx (workbook with route breakdown, concurrency model, and GPU math)
- redwood-cutover-runbook-v1.md (cutover checklist and owner map)

Notes: If your production model differs (e.g., 7B parameter family or different quant), numbers will change; please flag model variant early.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
